claim: The AI Voice Agents product is a separate app from the classic Obelix dashboard: it sits under a HOUSE OF AI section tagged NEW and its nav entry carries an external-link icon; the app has its own logo, white sidebar and rounded-card style.

Voice Agents app navigation is BUILD (Agents, Integrations with sub-items Tools and Database), MONITOR (Interactions, Analytics, Reports), MANAGE (Account, Model Configuration), plus a Credit Usage card; there is no Billing, Team, API keys, Numbers or Campaigns item inside this app.

Three different visual shells are in use for one product: the classic Obelix dashboard (blue sidebar, uppercase buttons), the Voice Agents app (white sidebar, indigo buttons) and the Engage app (a third narrow-sidebar style).

The account is unverified. The only onboarding guidance is a green banner in roughly 9-10 px text that packs five steps (Verify Number, Complete KYC, make a payment, Get an ExoPhone, done) into one sentence with a stray '!.'; there is no progress indicator or checklist.

A voice agent already existed on the trial account: 'Exotel-Voicebot', version v1 marked Stable and Live, 100% of traffic, created 10/20/2026 10:01:02 PM, languages English and Hindi, status Active. The Instinct notes say it was not created by the evaluation.

The pre-existing agent and the call-flow app 'voicebot-mum-prod-default-flow' (no ExoPhone attached) were most likely auto-provisioned at sign-up as a demo, because both carry 20 Oct dates and the agent's prompt is an Exotel product-demo persona. The create-agent form itself was never captured, so the true first-run path for building a new agent is unknown.
Agent detail has six tabs in this order: Workflow, Rollout, Knowledge Base, Database, Activity, Test; the header holds Freeze Agent, Talk to Agent (the only filled button) and Edit Agent.

The default workflow is a linear three-node graph: Bot, then a sub-agent named 'tool Calling Agent' (labelled Supervisor agent, described as 'Invokes the tool call and returns the response'), then End. Sub-Agents (1) is a section of the Bot panel.

Edit Agent opens the same workflow editor with Discard and 'Save and Rollout' (grey and disabled until a change), a version selector (v1 Stable Live) and an amber warning that a save may overwrite newer tool changes and to refresh after Database or KB sync, or open Rollout. Save and deploy are one action.

The top-level System Prompt section is not editable: it shows one sentence saying a prompt 'with strict guardrails is applied to ensure consistent, safe, and professional conversations'. The prompt text is not shown. Instinct reports by DOM inspection that no editor exists in edit mode either.

The editable prompt is the sub-agent 'Instruction', a raw monospace markdown box with '## Identity' and '## Objective' headings (the demo persona 'Exo'), inside a nested scroll area. Persona is free-form text, not a structured form.

[notes-only] General Settings on the live agent: Status Active; Greeting disabled; Mask Sensitive Data (PII masking) disabled; Enable Max Call Duration disabled. Values under the toggles (greeting text, duration) were not captured.

[notes-only] Denoiser is ON at enhancement level 0.8; VAD Configuration has no entry; Conversation Nudges use default wording, nudge after 7 s, up to 3 times, then end the call; Specialization Prompts none.

In the read-only Bot Details panel, Speech to Text shows 'azure' and Text to Speech shows 'Clyde' as collapsed rows; no latency, price, quality or language information appears inline beside either choice.

[notes-only] Edit mode shows: LLM Input Type Voice and Output Type Text; provider Google IN; model labelled Gemini 3 Flash with the config string 'gemini-2.5-flash-with-thinking'; STT 'Configuration Rule' Deepgram India plus an STT Engine field; TTS provider ElevenLabs with 183 tagged voices (e.g. Clyde en; Hindi collections, customer-care and BFSI-sales voices).

Which speech-to-text provider actually serves a call is unknown: Bot Details shows 'azure' while Edit mode shows a Deepgram India configuration rule, and the account-level Model Configuration list is empty for the last 30 days.

[notes-only] Webhooks: none; Intents configured on the live agent: Pricing, BotCapabilities, TechnicalDetails; Automated Call Intents: none; Query Definition: none. Intents are the classification and extraction mechanism.

[notes-only] Go Live offers 'Create appflow' (an App Bazaar call flow with the Voicebot applet pointed at the agent) or 'Use existing appflow'; the agent endpoint is a dp-endpoint URL pattern under voicebot.in.exotel.com. Going live is therefore a step in the classic console's flow layer.

Rollout shows versions with a traffic split: v1 with Stable and Live pills, 'This agent serves 100% on its current version', helper text to create a version to test a change on part of traffic, a 'Test this version' action and a collapsed 'Test Threads (0)'. No visible Create-version button.
The Test tab offers a Phone Call card ('Add a phone number to test your agent', no visible field or button) and a Web Call card tagged 'Coming soon' with a disabled button. No call was placed.

No simulation, eval suite, scripted test cases or AI QA scoring is visible anywhere in the Voice Agents app; testing is a live phone call, 'Test this version' or Test Threads (probably text, which is inferred from the name and from the earlier bundle finding).

Knowledge Base is a corpus table (Corpus ID, Corpus Name, Resource Name, Description, Last Trained, Status) with Active/Archived, Date and Status filters; the table is empty and shows no empty-state text or add button, so how a corpus is created is not visible.

Database is an account-level store of data tables the agent can look up; attaching happens from the agent's Database tab or Edit Agent while creating tables happens at Integrations > Database, a two-place flow. The account has no tables.

Integrations > Tools > Create is a 'Create Custom API Integration' form only: Integration Name, Description ('Helps AI understand when to use this integration'), Base Domain, HTTP Method (default GET), URL Path, then a separate 'Test API Integration' tab; Create is disabled until required fields are filled. No built-in tool catalogue is visible.
[notes-only] Call transfer and voicemail are not agent-level features; they are App Bazaar applets around the bot endpoint, and App Bazaar's own copy lists forwarding calls and taking voicemails.

App Bazaar shows a four-step funnel (Install, Test out with the trial number, Buy App, Connect to your company number) with all four pills styled alike, and a Custom Apps table of two apps with ExoPhone and App ID columns; one app has a TRIAL NUMBER attached.

Interactions (call logs) filters: filter-type select (Interaction ID), search, Date (default Oct 14 - Oct 21, last 7 days), Agent Name, Clear All; 20 rows per page; visible columns Interaction ID, Customer Number, Agent Name, Version, Date & Time, Duration with more to the right. The list is empty (no calls placed).
[notes-only] Interactions has two further columns beyond Duration, Completion Source and Intents.

The Analytics page renders as one blank grey panel with a browser broken-frame icon: no heading, message, filters or retry. Whether the failure is a capture artefact (blocked embedded frame) or a product fault is undetermined.
The Analytics view is most likely an embedded third-party dashboard (the earlier bundle teardown found Superset-backed analytics), which would explain the frame placeholder.

Reports are asynchronous and emailed: Report Type (Interactions), Date range default Oct 01 - Oct 21, comma-separated Email ID field, Send, helper 'Report will have latest data up to 30 mins from the current time', and a Report requests table (Report, Requested, Status). Other report types were not seen.

The Account page in the Voice Agents app holds one card: Concurrency 0 / 5 'across all agents on this account', with 'Last updated' time; raising it means writing to a vendor email address and is 'subject to monthly charges' with no price shown.
Credits show as 150 in the classic top bar and Credit Usage as 0 min in the Voice Agents sidebar; the unit relationship between the two (currency, minutes or both) is not explained in any capture.

[notes-only] Make a Payment offers online payment and bank transfer with a coupon field but is blocked behind a GST-details requirement ('we need GST details to proceed further'), so no plan or per-minute price is visible in the account.

No per-minute price, latency figure or quality rating for any model, voice or transcriber is displayed in any captured Voice Agents screen, unlike pickers that show latency and cost inline at other vendors.

The only conversation-control settings seen are Denoiser (0.8), VAD Configuration (empty), Conversation Nudges (7 s, 3 times, then end) and a disabled Max Call Duration toggle. No endpointing, interruption sensitivity, backchannel, reply-delay, DTMF or voicemail control was captured.
Nudge-then-hang-up at 7 s times 3 is the same order of magnitude as Bolna's 20 s hangup-on-silence (at least 21 s if nudges repeat every 7 s; the interval between nudges is unknown).
Whether Hinglish turn-taking, language hold, short-reply handling, DTMF, voicemail detection and AI disclosure work on Exotel is unknown without live calls; no capture bears on them.

Campaigns (classic console, Tools > Campaigns) has tabs Campaigns, Lists, Contacts, Settings and campaign types Call, SMS, WhatsApp, Dialer; the list is empty and its empty state reads 'No Results Found / Please try refining your search' even though no search was run.

Create Call Campaign is a single long form with Campaign Name (required) and an audience choice Static, Dynamic or Dynamic with CSV Upload, a Contact List multi-select limited to 5 lists, and a note that later list changes do not affect the campaign. Two error toasts, 'Unable to load Caller ID's' and 'Unable to load Lists', appeared on first load, so the form could not be completed.

[notes-only] Below the fold the wizard has: content as Read out via Text (TTS), Select a Flow, Create an IVR or Upload Audio; Caller ID; Call Type Transactional vs Promotional; Schedule Now or Later; retries 0-3 with interval, exponential backoff and retry on Busy, No Answer or Failed; Call Duplicate Numbers toggle; throttle Auto or Custom CPM; Campaign Status and Call Status callback URLs.

The enumerated wizard fields include a TRAI call-type choice but no per-contact consent field, no DND/NCPR scrub switch and no daily calling-window control, which fits the earlier finding that windows and consent are left to the buyer. Fields not enumerated by Instinct cannot be excluded.

The Address Book has no lists ('No matching Lists found'), one contact, and Export permissions ON by default for Agents and Supervisors; so even if the list loader worked, a new account has nothing to pick, and a list must be created first.

Contacts and lists appear in three places: Address Book, the Campaigns Lists and Contacts tabs, and Engage Contacts and List. Whether they are one store is unknown (Instinct states the Address Book is the store campaigns consume, which was not verified).
The Engage SMS campaigns page shows 'Complete KYC to use campaigns' inside the empty table while the 'Create SMS Campaign' button looks enabled; a Refresh button re-checks KYC status.

Co-workers and Groups: one user (account owner) with role Admin, phone flagged UNVERIFIED, INVITE button, drag-to-group model, groups Sales and Support with one user each; Address Book export permission refers to roles Agents and Supervisors. No SSO, MFA, audit or permission matrix is visible in the captures.

[notes-only] Other classic-console areas exist but were not opened: Impersonation, Company Info, Notifications, Co-worker Activity Log, Developer (API Settings), Access Control, Heartbeat, Audio Library. API Settings shows two pre-existing named API keys with masked tokens, account region Singapore and a subdomain api.exotel.com.

[notes-only] The account region is recorded as Singapore with API subdomain api.exotel.com while the voicebot app is on voicebot.in.exotel.com and the flow is named 'mum-prod'. This contradicts the earlier checklist that said to sign up on the India console and that the region is fixed at sign-up. Not verified from a screenshot (the API page capture was withheld).

[notes-only] SMS Settings carries DLT-style template placeholders, a 0/1000 template quota, a template-match tester and a Sender ID section; a Truecaller or Google verified-calling option and a NEW EXOPHONE purchase path exist but were not opened.

Evaluator-measured navigation timings in a cloud browser: classic console page load about 4.7 s; Campaigns v2 about 1.9 s plus about 5 s 'Checking access'; Voice Agents agents list about 3.0 s; cold first load of the Voice Agents app after SSO about 12-15 s; SSO hop about 12 s. These are page loads, not call latency.

The Voice Agents app has a Theme submenu under the avatar (Light, Dark, Match Browser, with layout thumbnails); the open menu clips the Database page subtitle, and the Database empty state says 'this agent' on an account-level page.

The Agents list shows Name, Goal (truncated), Language chips, Active Version ('v1 - stable'), Status, Created on, Last Modified and further columns cut off; a horizontal scrollbar overlaps the only data row.

Four capture labels mislead: exotel-02-voicebot-home is the agent Test tab, exotel-08-integrations is Integrations > Database, exotel-03-voicebot-workflow is a blurred content area with no readable settings, and the Analytics capture holds no analytics. No per-page text captures exist for Exotel, so below-the-fold settings rest on Instinct's notes alone.

Two captures show the account owner's full phone number in clear (co-workers card and address book row) and exotel-13's black-box redaction leaves the top edge of the digits partly visible; treat all three files as sensitive and do not publish them.

Reaching a bot-driven campaign spans surfaces: build and Go Live in the Voice Agents app, an appflow in App Bazaar, and the list, caller ID and schedule in classic Campaigns, with SMS and WhatsApp campaigns in a third app (Engage).
